154	// malformedChangeExportPath reports whether p targets the change-log
155	// collection's export shape but is not the collection's exact location
156	// (/v1/documents/{documentID}/changes): a trailing slash (an empty trailing
157	// segment) or extra path segments past the collection. The paged read and
158	// this export share that exact collection path; its terminal subresources
159	// (poll, compact, subscribe under the session family) have their own keyword
160	// guards, so only a genuinely unrecognized suffix reaches this check.
161	// ServeMux would answer it with a redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the
162	// change surface promises a JSON error and never a redirect. Empty segments
163	// are already rejected by the guard itself. The keyword is matched only past
164	// the documentID position, so a document literally named "changes" keeps its
165	// ordinary routes.
166	func malformedChangeExportPath(p string) bool {
167		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
168		if !ok {
169			return false
170		}
171		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
172		for i, seg := range segs {
173			if seg != "changes" || i == 0 {
174				continue
175			}
176			// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
177			// {documentID}/changes; the poll and compact subresources are their own
178			// endpoints and keep their own guards; the document-level subscription
179			// adds one trailing "subscribe" segment and keeps its own endpoint.
180			// Anything else (a trailing slash, an unrecognized extra segment) is a
181			// malformed 400.
182			if i == 1 {
183				collection := len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != ""
184				knownSubresource := len(segs) >= 3 &&
185					(segs[2] == "poll" || segs[2] == "compact" || segs[2] == "subscribe")
186				return !(collection || knownSubresource)
187			}
188			return false
189		}
190		return false
191	}
192	
193	// malformedSessionChangesPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
194	// change collection's shape but is not the collection's exact location
195	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes): extra path
196	// segments past the collection. The paged read and the interval export share
197	// that exact collection path; the subscribe subresource has its own endpoint
198	// and keyword guard, so only a genuinely unrecognized suffix reaches this
199	// check. ServeMux would answer it with a plain-text 404; the change surface
200	// promises a JSON 400 and never a redirect. Empty segments (doubled slashes,
201	// a trailing slash) are already rejected by the guard itself.
202	//
203	// "changes" is treated as the collection keyword only in the fourth segment,
204	// right after the document identifier; a session or document identifier
205	// literally named "changes" occupies an identifier position and keeps its
206	// ordinary routes.
207	func malformedSessionChangesPath(p string) bool {
208		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
209		if !ok {
210			return false
211		}
212		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
213		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
214		// has its own guard; "changes" there is an ordinary identifier, not this
215		// collection's keyword.
216		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
217			return false
218		}
219		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "changes" {
220			return false
221		}
222		// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
223		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes; the subscribe subresource
224		// adds one trailing "subscribe" segment and keeps its own guard; the long
225		// poll adds one trailing "poll" segment and keeps its own guard; the
226		// offline replay adds one trailing "replay" segment and keeps its own
227		// guard; the single-change merge adds one trailing "merge" segment and
228		// keeps its own guard; the change-log compaction adds one trailing
229		// "compact" segment and keeps its own guard. Anything else past the
230		// keyword is a malformed 400.
231		collection := len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != ""
232		subscribe := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "subscribe"
233		poll := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "poll"
234		replay := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "replay"
235		merge := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "merge"
236		compact := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "compact"
237		return !(collection || subscribe || poll || replay || merge || compact)
238	}

94	// NewHandlerWithReadiness builds the same public HTTP surface as NewHandler but
95	// answers every request — including GET /healthz — with a 503 JSON error until
96	// ready reports that the database is open and the listener is accepting
97	// connections. Once ready, responses are byte-for-byte what NewHandler emits;
98	// readiness is one-way, so a later flip back is not part of the contract.
99	func NewHandlerWithReadiness(s *app.App, ready func() bool) http.Handler {
100		h := NewHandler(s)
101		if ready == nil {
102			return h
103		}
104		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
105			if !ready() {
106				writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is not ready")
107				return
108			}
109			h.ServeHTTP(w, r)
110		})
111	}

113	// NewHandler builds the public HTTP surface backed by s.
114	func NewHandler(s *app.App) http.Handler {
115		mux := http.NewServeMux()

602	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
603	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
604	// plain-text 404.
605	//
606	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
607	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
608	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
609	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
610	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
611	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
612		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
613			p := r.URL.Path
614	
615			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
616			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
617			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
618				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
619			}
620	
621			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedDocumentDelete(r.Method, p) || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) || malformedPermissionPath(p) || malformedChangeExportPath(p) || malformedSessionChangesPath(p) || malformedSessionPollPath(p) || malformedSessionReplayPath(p) || malformedSessionMergePath(p) || malformedSessionCompactPath(p) || malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p) || malformedSessionRestorePath(p) {
622				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
623				return
624			}
625			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
626		})
627	}

629	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
630	// long-poll/replay/merge/restore/compaction endpoints but is not that
631	// endpoint's exact location: a missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra
632	// segments, or a "poll"/"replay"/"merge"/"restore"/"compact" segment in a
633	// position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
634	// 301 redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the new endpoints promise a JSON error
635	// and never a redirect, so every such path is a malformed 400.
636	//
637	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
638	// happen to be named "poll", "replay", "merge", "restore" or "compact" keep
639	// their ordinary merge/snapshot/changes routes.
640	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
641		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
642		if !ok {
643			return false
644		}
645		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
646	
647		// The named-snapshot-version subtree ({documentID}/snapshots/versions/...)
648		// owns its whole shape verdict through malformedSnapshotPath. A version
649		// name may coincide with a change keyword ("poll", "merge", "restore",
650		// "subscribe", "compact"), so none of the keyword loops below may judge a
651		// path inside that subtree; leave it to the snapshot guard.
652		if len(segs) >= 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "snapshots" && segs[2] == "versions" {
653			return false
654		}
655	
656		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
657		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
658		for i, seg := range segs {
659			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
660				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
661			}
662		}
663		// Document change subscription: "subscribe" must be exactly the third
664		// segment, after a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace
665		// has its own state/subscribe endpoint and its own guard, so a "subscribe"
666		// under crdt/ is not the change-subscription keyword.
667		for i, seg := range segs {
668			if seg == "subscribe" && i > 0 {
669				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
670					continue
671				}
672				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
673			}
674		}
675		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
676		// non-empty documentID.
677		for i, seg := range segs {
678			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
679				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
680			}
681		}
682		// Merge and restore endpoints: each keyword must be exactly the second
683		// segment, after a non-empty documentID (they are document-item
684		// subresources, unlike poll/compact which sit below the change
685		// collection). A keyword used as a version name inside the versions
686		// subtree was excluded by the early return above.
687		for _, keyword := range []string{"merge", "restore"} {
688			for i, seg := range segs {
689				if seg == keyword && i > 0 {
690					return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
691				}
692			}
693		}
694		// Compaction endpoint: "compact" must be exactly the third segment, after
695		// a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace has its own
696		// guard; "compact" there is the CRDT compaction keyword, not the
697		// change-log one.
698		for i, seg := range segs {
699			if seg == "compact" && i > 0 {
700				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
701					return false
702				}
703				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
704			}
705		}
706		return false
707	}

709	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
710	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
711	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
712	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
713	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
714	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
715	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
716	//
717	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
718	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
719	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
720	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
721	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
722	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
723		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
724		if !ok {
725			return false
726		}
727		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
728		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
729		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
730		// keyword.
731		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
732			return false
733		}
734		for i, seg := range segs {
735			if seg != "subscribe" {
736				continue
737			}
738			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
739			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
740			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
741				continue
742			}
743			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
744			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
745			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
746			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
747				segs[0] != "" &&
748				segs[1] == "documents" &&
749				segs[2] != "" &&
750				segs[3] == "changes" {
751				return false
752			}
753			return true
754		}
755		return false
756	}

758	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
759	// namespace but is not at one of its four exact locations:
760	//
761	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
762	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
763	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/compact
764	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
765	//
766	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"compact"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or
767	// a "crdt" segment in the keyword position (immediately past the document
768	// identifier) short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer
769	// those with a plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a
770	// JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
771	//
772	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
773	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
774	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
775	// keeps its ordinary routes. Likewise "compact" is the endpoint keyword only
776	// in the fifth segment; a session or document literally named "compact" is an
777	// ordinary identifier.
778	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
779		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
780		if !ok {
781			return false
782		}
783		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
784		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
785			return false
786		}
787		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit, the state read and the
788		// compaction are all exactly
789		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state,compact}; the
790		// subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
791		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
792			segs[0] != "" &&
793			segs[2] != "" &&
794			segs[4] == "ops"
795		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
796			segs[0] != "" &&
797			segs[2] != "" &&
798			segs[4] == "state"
799		validCompact := len(segs) == 5 &&
800			segs[0] != "" &&
801			segs[2] != "" &&
802			segs[4] == "compact"
803		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
804			segs[0] != "" &&
805			segs[2] != "" &&
806			segs[4] == "state" &&
807			segs[5] == "subscribe"
808		return !(validOps || validState || validCompact || validSubscribe)
809	}

821	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
822	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
823	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
824	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
825	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
826	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
827	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
828		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
829		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
830			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
831			return false
832		}
833	
834		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
835		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
836		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
837			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
838			return false
839		}
840		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
841		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
842			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
843			return false
844		}
845		return true
846	}

937

939		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
940			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
941			return

944		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)

950		}

952		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
953			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
954			return
955		}

957		if req.DeviceID == "" {
958			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
959			return
960		}
961		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
962			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
963			return
964		}
965	
966		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
967		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
968		for i, c := range req.Changes {
969			if c.ID == "" {
970				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
971				return
972			}
973			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
974				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
975				return
976			}
977			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
978				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
979				return
980			}
981			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
982			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: c.Payload}
983		}

996			return

1254	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
1255	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
1256	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
1257		if raw == "" {
1258			return 0, false
1259		}
1260		for _, c := range raw {
1261			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1262				return 0, false
1263			}
1264		}
1265		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1266		if err != nil {
1267			return 0, false
1268		}
1269		return n, true
1270	}

1272	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1273	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1274		var n int64
1275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1276			return 0, false
1277		}
1278		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1279		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1280		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1281		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1282			return 0, false
1283		}
1284		for _, c := range trimmed {
1285			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1286				return 0, false
1287			}
1288		}
1289		return n, true
1290	}
1291	
1292	// parsePositiveInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 1. Zero, floats,
1293	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1294	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1295		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
1296		if !ok || n < 1 {
1297			return 0, false
1298		}
1299		return n, true
1300	}

1303	// array or a scalar).
1304	func isJSONObject(raw json.RawMessage) bool {

1306		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
1307			return false
1308		}
1309		return true
1310	}

1394	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1395	// change collection the session reads page:
1396	//
1397	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1398	//
1399	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1400	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1401	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1402	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1403	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1404	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1405	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1406	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1407	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1408	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1409	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.
1410	func handleSessionPostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1411		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1412		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1413	
1414		var req sessionPostRequest
1415		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1416			return
1417		}
1418		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
1419			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1420			return
1421		}
1422	
1423		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
1424		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
1425		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1426			if c.ID == "" {
1427				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1428				return
1429			}
1430			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1431				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1432				return
1433			}
1434			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1435				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1436				return
1437			}
1438			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
1439			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, Payload: c.Payload}
1440		}
1441	
1442		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1443		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.
1444		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1445		if err != nil {
1446			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1447				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1448				return
1449			}
1450			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1451			return
1452		}
1453		for i := range changes {
1454			changes[i].DeviceID = deviceID
1455		}
1456	
1457		results, err := s.PostSessionChanges(documentID, changes)
1458		if err != nil {
1459			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1460			switch {
1461			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1462				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and
1463				// the commit; its cascade removed the session too, so the
1464				// identity the caller used no longer exists.
1465				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1466			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1467				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1468			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1469				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1470					"error":      "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1471					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1472				})
1473			default:
1474				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
1475			}
1476			return
1477		}
1478	
1479		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1480	}

1575		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})

1580	// session's owning device resolved from the path, so a stray deviceId is
1581	// decoded and ignored like every other unknown field.
1582	type sessionMergeRequest struct {
1583		BaseCursor json.RawMessage `json:"baseCursor"`

1585	}

1587	// handleSessionMergeChange is the session-scoped single-change merge entry,
1588	// the session view's counterpart to
1589	// POST /v1/documents/{documentID}/merge, mounted one segment below the change
1590	// collection:
1591	//
1592	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/merge
1593	//
1594	// The body carries only baseCursor and one change; the calling device is the
1595	// session's owning device resolved from the path with the same identity rule as
1596	// the session reads, exports, commits, replays, polls and subscriptions — no
1597	// new credential is introduced, and a stray deviceId in the body is ignored
1598	// like any other unknown field. The merge judgment, success body and cursor
1599	// space are byte-identical to the document-level merge: a single result naming
1600	// the id, its three-way outcome ("applied", "merged" or "idempotent") and the
1601	// cursor it received, with the original result attached only when nothing was
1602	// created. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400), session
1603	// existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict is taken
1604	// inside the merge transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing — and the
1605	// in-transaction merge failures (a stale or compacted base cursor, an
1606	// id/payload/source mismatch, a key collision or a non-object later payload)
1607	// answer 400 or 409 with zero writes.
1608	func handleSessionMergeChange(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1609		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1610		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

1612		var req sessionMergeRequest

1615		}

1617		// strings, booleans or null).

1624			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor must be a non-negative integer")
1625			return
1626		}
1627		if req.Change == nil {
1628			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change must be an object")
1629			return
1630		}
1631		if req.Change.ID == "" {
1632			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.id must be a non-empty string")
1633			return
1634		}
1635		if len(req.Change.Payload) == 0 || !isJSONObject(req.Change.Payload) {
1636			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.payload must be a JSON object")

1638		}

1641		// malformed merge against an unknown session is still a 400.
1642		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)

1644			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1645				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1646				return
1647			}
1648			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1649			return
1650		}

1652		result, err := s.MergeSessionChange(documentID, baseCursor, events.Change{
1653			ID:       req.Change.ID,
1654			DeviceID: deviceID,
1655			Payload:  req.Change.Payload,
1656		})
1657		if err != nil {

1659			switch {
1660			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):

1662				// merge; its cascade removed the session too, so the identity the
1663				// caller used no longer exists.
1664				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1665			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1666				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1667			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStaleCursor):
1668				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is unknown or greater than the current cursor")
1669			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrCompactedBase):

1672				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "merge conflicts with existing changes: "+conflict.ID)

1682	// parseChangesQuery parses the shared after/limit pagination parameters,

1685	// cannot drift apart.
1686	func parseChangesQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (after, limit int64, ok bool) {
1687		q := r.URL.Query()
1688	
1689		after = 0
1690		if raw := q.Get("after"); raw != "" {
1691			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1692			if err != nil || v < 0 {
1693				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "after must be a non-negative integer")

1695			}

1697		}
1698	
1699		limit = defaultListLimit
1700		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
1701			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1702			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
1703				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
1704				return 0, 0, false

1712	// writeChangesPage renders a change listing page in the shared response shape.
1713	func writeChangesPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64) {
1714		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1715			"changes":    changes,
1716			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1717		})
1718	}
1719	
1720	// parsePollWaitMs parses the long-poll waitMs query parameter, writing the
1721	// documented 400 on an illegal value. It accepts an integer in 0..30000
1722	// milliseconds and defaults to 0 when the parameter is absent; a value outside
1723	// the range, a fraction, an exponent or any non-numeric value is rejected. It
1724	// is shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped long polls so their wait
1725	// semantics cannot drift apart.
1726	func parsePollWaitMs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int64, bool) {
1727		var waitMs int64
1728		if raw := r.URL.Query().Get("waitMs"); raw != "" {
1729			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1730			if err != nil || v < 0 || v > maxPollWaitMillis {
1731				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "waitMs must be an integer between 0 and 30000")
1732				return 0, false
1733			}
1734			waitMs = v
1735		}
1736		return waitMs, true
1737	}
1738	
1739	// writePollPage renders a long-poll result in the shared response shape: the
1740	// ordinary page plus a timedOut flag, with the top-level keys in the fixed
1741	// changes, nextCursor, timedOut order.
1742	func writePollPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool) {
1743		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1744			"changes":    changes,
1745			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1746			"timedOut":   timedOut,
1747		})
1748	}
1749	
1750	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
1751		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
1752		w.WriteHeader(status)
1753		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
1754	}
1755	
1756	func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, message string) {
1757		writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": message})
1758	}

1760	// handlePollChanges is the long-polling entry over the change log.
1761	//
1762	// Query params share the existing change-read constraints: after is a
1763	// non-negative cursor (default 0) and limit is 1..1000 (default 100); waitMs
1764	// is 0..30000 (default 0). Rows already past after return immediately; a known
1765	// document caught up to after parks until the first new commit or the wait
1766	// deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at once.
1767	// The response shape is the ordinary page plus a timedOut flag; a deadline
1768	// expiry echoes the caller's cursor and never advances it. A client
1769	// disconnect simply stops the wait and writes nothing.
1770	func handlePollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1771		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1772	
1773		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1774		if !ok {
1775			return
1776		}
1777		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)

1779			return
1780		}
1781	
1782		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1783			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1784		)

1786		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):

1788			return
1789		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1790			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1791			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1792			return
1793		case err != nil:
1794			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1795			return
1796		}
1797	
1798		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)

1801	// handleSessionPollChanges is the session-scoped long-poll continuation over
1802	// the same change collection the session reads page:
1803	//
1804	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/poll
1805	//
1806	// The request is a GET with no body; the calling device is the session's
1807	// owning device resolved with the same identity rule as the session reads,
1808	// exports, commits and subscriptions. Query parameters and the success body are
1809	// identical to GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/changes/poll — after (default 0),
1810	// limit (default 100, 1..1000) and waitMs (default 0, 0..30000), answered with
1811	// changes, nextCursor and timedOut in that order, rows ascending by cursor.
1812	//
1813	// Rows already past after return immediately with timedOut=false; a known
1814	// document caught up to after parks until the first commit through any write
1815	// path (session batch commit, document commit, merge, restore, replay) or the
1816	// wait deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at
1817	// once and never parks. A deadline expiry returns the empty page, echoes the
1818	// caller's after and sets timedOut=true without advancing the cursor. Checks
1819	// run in the fixed order request shape and parameters (400), session
1820	// existence (404), document permission (403); a rejected request exposes no
1821	// change content. A client disconnect simply cancels the wait and writes
1822	// nothing; while the service is shutting down the parked request answers a
1823	// JSON 503.
1824	func handleSessionPollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1825		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1826		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1827	
1828		// Parameter shape precedes the session lookup, matching the session paged
1829		// read's ordering: a malformed after/limit/waitMs against an unknown
1830		// session is still a 400.
1831		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1832		if !ok {
1833			return
1834		}
1835		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1836		if !ok {
1837			return
1838		}
1839	
1840		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1841		if err != nil {
1842			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1843				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1844				return
1845			}
1846			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1847			return
1848		}
1849	
1850		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
1851		if err != nil {
1852			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
1853			return
1854		}
1855		if !authorized {
1856			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1857			return
1858		}
1859	
1860		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1861			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1862		)
1863		switch {
1864		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1865			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1866			return
1867		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1868			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1869			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1870			return
1871		case err != nil:
1872			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1873			return
1874		}
1875	
1876		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1877	}
1878	
1879	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
1880	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
1881	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
1882	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
1883	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
1884	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
1885	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
1886	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
1887	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1888		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1889	
1890		var req replayRequest
1891		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1892			return
1893		}
1894		if req.DeviceID == "" {
1895			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
1896			return
1897		}
1898		if req.Operations == nil {
1899			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1900			return
1901		}
1902		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1903			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1904			return
1905		}
1906	
1907		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1908		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
1909		for i, op := range req.Operations {
1910			if op.ID == "" {
1911				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1912				return
1913			}
1914			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
1915				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
1916				return
1917			}
1918			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
1919				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
1920				return
1921			}
1922			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1923			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
1924		}
1925	
1926		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
1927		if err != nil {
1928			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1929			switch {
1930			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1931				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
1932			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1933				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1934			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1935				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1936					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1937					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1938				})
1939			default:
1940				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
1941			}
1942			return
1943		}
1944	
1945		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1946	}

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// ErrVersionConflict reports that a version registration or rename cannot be
131	// applied: the version name is already bound to a different snapshot cursor,
132	// or the requested bind would move an existing name (and zero writes is the
133	// required outcome). The caller maps it to 409.
134	type ErrVersionConflict struct {
135		Name string
136	}
137	
138	func (e *ErrVersionConflict) Error() string {
139		return fmt.Sprintf("snapshot version %q is bound to another cursor", e.Name)
140	}
141	
142	// ErrVersionNotFound reports that no snapshot version of the document carries
143	// the requested name. The caller maps it to 404.
144	var ErrVersionNotFound = errors.New("snapshot version not found")
145	
146	// SnapshotVersion is one row of a ListSnapshotVersions result: the version
147	// name together with the snapshot cursor it points at.
148	type SnapshotVersion struct {
149		Name   string `json:"name"`
150		Cursor int64  `json:"snapshotCursor"`
151	}
152	
153	// VersionResult reports the outcome of registering or renaming a snapshot
154	// version: the version name and the snapshot cursor it is bound to. An
155	// idempotent registration returns the same body as the first registration.
156	type VersionResult struct {
157		Name   string `json:"name"`
158		Cursor int64  `json:"snapshotCursor"`

9	// DocumentExists reports whether documentID is a known document rather than an
10	// empty namespace: it has any online change row, or a compaction boundary from
11	// a log that was (fully or partially) trimmed.
12	func (s *Service) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
13		var known bool
14		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
15			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)
16			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?)`,
17			documentID, documentID,
18		).Scan(&known); err != nil {
19			return false, err
20		}
21		return known, nil
22	}
23	
24	// ListChanges returns at most limit changes for documentID whose cursor is
25	// greater than after and still online, in cursor order, together with the
26	// cursor to pass as the next after value. An unknown document yields an empty
27	// list and cursor 0; a known document with no rows past after yields
28	// nextCursor == max(after, boundary), so a caller positioned inside the
29	// trimmed range resumes from the compaction boundary.
30	func (s *Service) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]ListedChange, int64, error) {
31		rows, err := s.db.Query(
32			`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
33			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor > ?
34			 ORDER BY cursor ASC
35			 LIMIT ?`,
36			documentID, after, limit,
37		)
38		if err != nil {
39			return nil, 0, err
40		}
41		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
42	
43		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
44		var maxCursor int64 = after
45		for rows.Next() {
46			var c ListedChange
47			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
48				return nil, 0, err
49			}
50			out = append(out, c)
51			maxCursor = c.Cursor
52		}
53		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
54			return nil, 0, err
55		}
56	
57		// Distinguish an unknown document from a known one with nothing new:
58		// unknown documents must report nextCursor 0, while a known document
59		// reports the greater of after and the compaction boundary.
60		if len(out) == 0 {
61			known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
62			if err != nil {
63				return nil, 0, err
64			}
65			if !known {
66				return out, 0, nil
67			}
68			boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(s.db, documentID)
69			if err != nil {
70				return nil, 0, err
71			}
72			if boundary > maxCursor {
73				maxCursor = boundary
74			}
75		}
76		return out, maxCursor, nil
77	}

79	// ExportChanges returns every change of documentID whose cursor lies in the
80	// closed interval [from, to] and is still in the online log, in ascending
81	// cursor order. When to is nil no upper bound is applied. An unknown document,
82	// or a range without any online change — including one that lies entirely
83	// inside the trimmed region — yields an empty list and no error: the export is
84	// a read that misses like any other. The (document_id, cursor) unique index
85	// guarantees a cursor appears at most once.
86	//
87	// The single SELECT runs as one SQLite statement over the serialized
88	// connection, so a batch committed concurrently is observed either with all of
89	// its rows or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no transaction,
90	// writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a cursor, produce
91	// a change record or wake a parked poll. Each returned row is the same record
92	// the paged read emits at that cursor.
93	func (s *Service) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ListedChange, error) {
94		var (
95			rows *sql.Rows
96			err  error
97		)
98		if to == nil {
99			rows, err = s.db.Query(
100				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
101				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
102				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
103				documentID, from,
104			)
105		} else {
106			rows, err = s.db.Query(
107				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
108				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
109				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
110				documentID, from, *to,
111			)
112		}
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
117	
118		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
119		for rows.Next() {
120			var c ListedChange
121			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
122				return nil, err
123			}
124			out = append(out, c)
125		}
126		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
127			return nil, err
128		}
129		return out, nil
130	}
131	
132	// WaitForChanges blocks until documentID has a change with cursor greater than
133	// after, a change is committed while waiting, wait elapses, ctx is canceled
134	// (the client disconnected) or the service stops. It then returns the current
135	// page of up to limit changes exactly as ListChanges would, with timedOut=true
136	// only when the wait deadline expired with no new rows.
137	//
138	// Registration precedes the first query: a commit landing between the read and
139	// the park still notifies a registered channel, so no change is missed.
140	//
141	// An unknown document is never parked on: it returns immediately with an empty
142	// list and nextCursor 0, timedOut=false. Data already past after is likewise
143	// returned immediately. wait <= 0 is an immediately expired deadline.
144	func (s *Service) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) (changes []ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool, err error) {
145		ch, remove := s.registerWait(documentID)
146		defer remove()
147	
148		changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
149		if err != nil || len(changes) > 0 {
150			return changes, nextCursor, false, err
151		}
152	
153		// Empty page: distinguish an unknown document (immediate empty/0, never
154		// parked on) from a known document caught up to after.
155		known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
156		if err != nil || !known {
157			return changes, 0, false, err
158		}
159	
160		// Known document, nothing new: a zero wait is an immediately expired
161		// deadline; ListChanges already echoes nextCursor == after.
162		if wait <= 0 {
163			return changes, nextCursor, true, nil
164		}
165	
166		timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
167		defer timer.Stop()
168	
169		select {
170		case <-ch:
171			// Woken by a committed change, a whole-document deletion, or
172			// InterruptWaits. A deleted document is an unknown document now: answer
173			// an empty page at cursor 0 with timedOut=false rather than reporting a
174			// deadline expiry. Any other empty re-read keeps the old timeout shape.
175			s.mu.Lock()
176			closing := s.closed
177			s.mu.Unlock()
178			if closing {
179				return nil, 0, false, ErrStoreClosing
180			}
181			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
182			if err != nil {
183				return nil, 0, false, err
184			}
185			if len(changes) == 0 {
186				known, knownErr := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
187				if knownErr != nil {
188					return nil, 0, false, knownErr
189				}
190				if !known {
191					return changes, 0, false, nil
192				}
193			}
194			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
195		case <-timer.C:
196			// Timeout with no new rows: echo the caller's cursor without
197			// advancing it. The document was known above, so ListChanges returns
198			// nextCursor == after for an empty page.
199			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
200			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
201		case <-ctx.Done():
202			return nil, 0, false, ctx.Err()
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// registerWait parks a channel for documentID and returns it together with a
207	// removal function. The channel is closed on the next committed change to the
208	// document, or when the service stops.
209	func (s *Service) registerWait(documentID string) (ch chan struct{}, remove func()) {
210		ch = make(chan struct{}, 1)
211	
212		s.mu.Lock()
213		defer s.mu.Unlock()
214		if s.closed {
215			// Shutdown beat the registration: signal immediately so the caller does
216			// not park on a channel nobody will close.
217			close(ch)
218			return ch, func() {}
219		}
220		s.nextWait++
221		id := s.nextWait
222		set := s.waits[documentID]
223		if set == nil {
224			set = make(map[uint64]chan struct{})
225			s.waits[documentID] = set
226		}
227		set[id] = ch
228		return ch, func() {
229			s.mu.Lock()
230			if set, ok := s.waits[documentID]; ok {
231				delete(set, id)
232				if len(set) == 0 {
233					delete(s.waits, documentID)
234				}
235			}
236			s.mu.Unlock()
237		}
238	}
239	
240	// notifyWaiters signals every long poll parked on documentID and every
241	// subscription open on it. It is called only after a change-bearing
242	// transaction has committed, so parked readers observe the new rows when they
243	// re-query and pushed frames describe committed changes.
244	func (s *Service) notifyWaiters(documentID string) {
245		s.mu.Lock()
246		set := s.waits[documentID]
247		delete(s.waits, documentID)
248		s.mu.Unlock()
249		for _, ch := range set {
250			close(ch)
251		}
252		s.signalSubscribers(documentID)
253	}

1	// Change-log compaction moves the old end of a document's change log out of
2	// the online tables without touching the cursor space the log shares with
3	// every write path.
4	//
5	// The compaction boundary is the greatest cursor that has a saved snapshot
6	// (zero when the document has none): everything at or below it is reproducible
7	// from a snapshot plus the surviving tail, so those rows leave the online log.
8	// A trimmed change is not forgotten, though — its id keeps a small canonical
9	// summary (the originating device, a digest of the payload and, for a restore,
10	// the snapshot it came from, plus the cursor it was first assigned) so the
11	// submission layer keeps answering idempotency and conflict exactly as before.
12	// The summary never participates in reads: pagination, long polling and
13	// subscriptions simply no longer see the trimmed rows, and the summary's
14	// fixed size means storage does not grow back to the pre-compaction shape.
15	//
16	// Compaction itself is not a change: it allocates no cursor, writes no change
17	// record and wakes no waiter or subscriber. The cursor space never resets —
18	// the next allocated cursor is one past the greater of the online maximum and
19	// the boundary — and the boundary, the summaries and the read results are
20	// durable across restarts.
21	
22	package events
23	
24	import (
25		"bytes"
26		"crypto/sha256"
27		"database/sql"
28		"encoding/json"
29		"errors"
30	
31		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
32	)
33	
34	// CompactChanges moves every change of documentID whose cursor is at or below
35	// the compaction boundary out of the online log, in one serialized
36	// transaction, and returns the boundary together with the number of changes
37	// removed by this call.
38	//
39	// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, or zero when the
40	// document has no snapshot — compacting a snapshot-less or unknown document
41	// succeeds and removes nothing. The gate is enforced before any content is
42	// observed, exactly as in ReplayChanges: an unregistered device yields
43	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields store.ErrPermissionDenied,
44	// and neither touches any state.
45	//
46	// Each trimmed id keeps its canonical summary (device, payload digest, restore
47	// provenance and first cursor) so re-posting it stays idempotent and a
48	// differing re-post stays a conflict. Compaction is idempotent: a repeat finds
49	// the same boundary, trims nothing and reports zero removed. It commits no
50	// change row, allocates no cursor and notifies no waiter or subscriber.
51	func (s *Service) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
52		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
53		if err != nil {
54			return 0, 0, err
55		}
56		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
57	
58		// Registration and permission are enforced before any change content is
59		// observed, so a rejected compaction cannot reveal anything.
60		if s.gate != nil {
61			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
62				return 0, 0, err
63			}
64		}
65	
66		// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, 0 when the
67		// document has none (an unknown document included).
68		if err := tx.QueryRow(
69			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?`,
70			documentID,
71		).Scan(&boundary); err != nil {
72			return 0, 0, err
73		}
74		stored, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
75		if err != nil {
76			return 0, 0, err
77		}
78		if boundary <= stored {
79			// Nothing new to trim (a repeat compaction, or a snapshot-less
80			// document): report the standing boundary and remove nothing.
81			return stored, 0, tx.Commit()
82		}
83	
84		// Collect the rows leaving the online log before deleting them: each one
85		// first moves its canonical summary into the identity table.
86		type trimmed struct {
87			cursor  int64
88			id      string
89			device  string
90			payload []byte
91		}
92		rows, err := tx.Query(
93			`SELECT cursor, id, device_id, payload FROM changes
94			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?
95			 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
96			documentID, boundary,
97		)
98		if err != nil {
99			return 0, 0, err
100		}
101		var dropping []trimmed
102		for rows.Next() {
103			var t trimmed
104			if err := rows.Scan(&t.cursor, &t.id, &t.device, &t.payload); err != nil {
105				_ = rows.Close()
106				return 0, 0, err
107			}
108			dropping = append(dropping, t)
109		}
110		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
111			_ = rows.Close()
112			return 0, 0, err
113		}
114		_ = rows.Close()
115	
116		for _, t := range dropping {
117			// A restored change also carries its provenance into the summary, so a
118			// repeated restore keeps its idempotency/conflict decision.
119			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
120			err := tx.QueryRow(
121				`SELECT snapshot_cursor FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
122				documentID, t.id,
123			).Scan(&restoredFrom)
124			switch {
125			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
126				restoredFrom = sql.NullInt64{}
127			case err != nil:
128				return 0, 0, err
129			}
130			digest, err := payloadDigest(t.payload)
131			if err != nil {
132				return 0, 0, err
133			}
134			if _, err := tx.Exec(
135				`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO change_identities
136					(document_id, id, device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from)
137				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
138				documentID, t.id, t.device, digest, t.cursor, restoredFrom,
139			); err != nil {
140				return 0, 0, err
141			}
142		}
143	
144		if _, err := tx.Exec(
145			`DELETE FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_cursor <= ?`,
146			documentID, boundary,
147		); err != nil {
148			return 0, 0, err
149		}
150		if _, err := tx.Exec(
151			`DELETE FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?`,
152			documentID, boundary,
153		); err != nil {
154			return 0, 0, err
155		}
156		if _, err := tx.Exec(
157			`INSERT INTO change_boundaries (document_id, boundary) VALUES (?, ?)
158			 ON CONFLICT (document_id) DO UPDATE SET boundary = excluded.boundary`,
159			documentID, boundary,
160		); err != nil {
161			return 0, 0, err
162		}
163	
164		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
165			return 0, 0, err
166		}
167		// Compaction is not a change: no waiter is woken and no subscriber is
168		// signaled, because no new change exists to observe.
169		return boundary, int64(len(dropping)), nil
170	}
171	
172	// boundaryOfTx returns the stored compaction boundary of documentID, or zero
173	// when the document was never compacted.
174	func boundaryOfTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (int64, error) {
175		var boundary int64
176		err := q.QueryRow(
177			`SELECT boundary FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?`,
178			documentID,
179		).Scan(&boundary)
180		switch {
181		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
182			return 0, nil
183		case err != nil:
184			return 0, err
185		default:
186			return boundary, nil
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// currentCursorTx returns the document's high-water mark: the greatest online
191	// cursor, or the compaction boundary when every change up to it has left the
192	// online log. The cursor space never resets, so a fully trimmed document
193	// continues from its boundary rather than from zero.
194	func currentCursorTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (int64, error) {
195		var maxOnline int64
196		if err := tx.QueryRow(
197			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
198			documentID,
199		).Scan(&maxOnline); err != nil {
200			return 0, err
201		}
202		boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
203		if err != nil {
204			return 0, err
205		}
206		if boundary > maxOnline {
207			maxOnline = boundary
208		}
209		return maxOnline, nil
210	}
211	
212	// payloadDigest renders a payload in the canonical form JSONEqual compares —
213	// the decoded value re-encoded, so 1 and 1.0 or reordered object keys digest
214	// alike — and hashes it. The digest is the fixed-size stand-in for the payload
215	// in a trimmed change's retained summary.
216	func payloadDigest(payload json.RawMessage) ([]byte, error) {
217		var v any
218		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &v); err != nil {
219			return nil, err
220		}
221		canonical, err := json.Marshal(v)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225		sum := sha256.Sum256(canonical)
226		return sum[:], nil
227	}
228	
229	// resolveTrimmedIdentity answers the submission question for an id whose
230	// online row is absent because compaction trimmed it. It returns found=true
231	// and the id's first cursor when the retained summary matches the incoming
232	// device and payload (an idempotent re-post), an *ErrConflict when a retained
233	// summary exists but differs, and found=false when no summary was retained (a
234	// genuinely new id).
235	func resolveTrimmedIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, c Change) (found bool, cursor int64, err error) {
236		var device string
237		var digest []byte
238		err = tx.QueryRow(
239			`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
240			documentID, c.ID,
241		).Scan(&device, &digest, &cursor)
242		switch {
243		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
244			return false, 0, nil
245		case err != nil:
246			return false, 0, err
247		}
248	
249		incoming, err := payloadDigest(c.Payload)
250		if err != nil {
251			return false, 0, err
252		}
253		if device != c.DeviceID || !bytes.Equal(digest, incoming) {
254			return false, 0, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
255		}
256		return true, cursor, nil
257	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
84		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
85	
86		return &App{
87			Store:    kernel,
88			events:   eventService,
89			crdt:     crdtService,
90			Authz:    permissions,
91			pushSubs: push.NewRegistry(),
92		}, nil
93	}

286	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
287	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
288	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its

291	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
292	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
293	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
294	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
295	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.

298	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live

300	// immediately, stickily.
301	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
302		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
303		if err != nil {
304			return err
305		}
306		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
307	
308		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
309			return err
310		}
311		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
312			return err
313		}
314		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
315			return err
316		}

318		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
319		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
320		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.

327	
328	// DeleteDocument removes a registered device's whole document in one
329	// serialized, synchronously committed transaction. The calling device is
330	// declared by deviceId — no new authentication is introduced.
331	//
332	// The fixed verdict order is taken inside the transaction, before any cleanup:
333	//
334	//   - an unregistered device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and writes
335	//     nothing;
336	//   - a device whose permission for the document was revoked yields
337	//     store.ErrPermissionDenied (403) and no cleanup runs;
338	//   - a document with no durable data anywhere — never created or already
339	//     deleted — yields events.ErrDocumentNotFound (404) and writes nothing.
340	//
341	// On success every row of the document is removed as one judgment: its online
342	// and trimmed change log, the retained idempotency summaries, its snapshots
343	// and named snapshot-version markers, its CRDT state and the per-document
344	// permission ledger. The same id is a brand-new document afterward — the
345	// cursor space restarts at 1 — and inherits no history or version names.
346	// Concurrent deletes commit at most once because the existence verdict and
347	// the deletions share one immediate transaction on the single connection.
348	//
349	// Only after the commit is durable are the document's live subscriptions
350	// ended (close code 4420 on both push channels) and dropped from the
351	// management registry; other documents' and devices' connections are
352	// untouched.
353	func (a *App) DeleteDocument(documentID, deviceID string) error {
354		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
355		if err != nil {
356			return err
357		}
358		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
359	
360		// Registration first, then permission, both before any document content
361		// is observed: a rejected delete reveals nothing and cleans nothing.
362		if err := a.Authz.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
363			return err
364		}
365	
366		eventsExist, err := a.events.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
367		if err != nil {
368			return err
369		}
370		crdtExist, err := a.crdt.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
371		if err != nil {
372			return err
373		}
374		// A ledger-only deviation row also counts as document data, so a document
375		// whose only durable trace is a grant/revoke still deletes cleanly and the
376		// re-created id inherits no authorization state.
377		ledgerExist, err := a.Authz.DocumentHasRowsTx(tx, documentID)
378		if err != nil {
379			return err
380		}
381		if !eventsExist && !crdtExist && !ledgerExist {
382			return events.ErrDocumentNotFound
383		}
384	
385		if err := a.events.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		if err := a.crdt.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
389			return err
390		}
391		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
392			return err
393		}
394	
395		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
396			return err
397		}
398	
399		// End the document's live subscriptions on both channels and drop them
400		// from the management registry only after the cleanup is durable: the
401		// close is one-shot per connection, so a client re-subscribing to the
402		// now-fresh id opens a new connection and never reopens the ended ones.
403		a.events.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
404		a.crdt.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
405		a.CloseDocumentPush(documentID)
406		return nil
407	}
